1 - `id`: 0076-sleep-cycle-promoted-a-gandalf-lesson-into-a-live-bug
2 - `skill`: ecgberht@v1.2.0
3 - `situation`: a sleep cycle promotes a lesson from one skill's journal and it lands on a live defect in another
4 - `context`: first real sleep cycle over the Foundry+trio corpus, 2026-08-04, run after
5   514 journal files had accumulated with no cycle ever executed.
6 - `observation`:
7 
8   **A lesson from gandalf's journal found a bug shipped in Ecgberht hours earlier.**
9   Gandalf 0274+0275 clustered (2 distinct contexts) on whole-project brownfield reads,
10   and 0275's named fix was: a `main()` guard comparing `resolve(argv[1])` to the module's
11   own path is a SILENT NO-OP through a junction — two spellings of one file, never equal,
12   so `main()` never runs and the process exits 0 with empty stdout.
13 
14   Ecgberht is REGISTERED as a junction (`~/.claude/skills/ecgberht -> C:\dev\Ecgberht`),
15   so the canonical host path is exactly the spelling that triggers it. Verified live:
16   `node ~/.claude/skills/ecgberht/bin/ecgberht.mjs status --project …` printed NOTHING
17   and exited 0. Same for `bin/steward.mjs` — which I had written that same day, copying
18   the defective guard from `bin/ecgberht.mjs` without examining it. That is the second
19   time in two days a defect propagated because I copied a working-looking construct
20   (the first was the Foreman launcher's inverted model seats, journal foreman/0098).
21 
22   Fixed by realpathing both sides (`engine/direct-invocation.mjs`), exported, used by
23   both CLIs, and pinned by `test/wh2-junction-invocation.test.mjs`, which reaches the
24   CLIs through a real junction and fails if either guard regresses.
25 
26   **Two process notes worth more than the bug.** (1) My first version of that test used
27   `t.skip()` when a symlink could not be created — and the repo's w48 guard correctly
28   failed the build: a silently-skipped test is indistinguishable from a passing one. The
29   skip was unnecessary (directory junctions need no privilege), so the test now fails
30   loudly instead. (2) My first two journal PARSERS were wrong (a JS regex with `\Z`,
31   which matches a literal Z, so the last field never terminated) and reported 0-32
32   entries out of 514. A parser bug and a genuinely quiet corpus produce IDENTICAL output
33   — "no candidates" — which is precisely how a broken improvement loop stays invisible.
34 - `outcome`: worked — 2 lessons promoted to gandalf LESSONS.md, 1 live defect fixed in
35   two CLIs, gate 1205/0
36 - `provenance`: genuine-execution
37 
38 ## Lesson (one line)
39 
40 **Run the sleep cycle across skills, not within one — the corroborated lesson from one
41 skill's journal is often a live, unnoticed defect in another — and never trust a
42 "0 candidates" cycle until you have printed parsed-vs-total, because a broken reader and
43 a quiet corpus look exactly alike.**
